system_note: What was billed: Diagnoses included I26.99 (PE) as principal, I46.9 (cardiac arrest, MCC), G93.1 (anoxic brain damage, MCC), J96.01 (acute respiratory failure with hypoxia, MCC), I50.30 (heart failure), N17.9 (AKI, CC), I82.401 (R LE DVT, POA=N), E03.9, F32.9, and Z-codes for history/implant/anticoagulant use. Procedures billed include 0BH17EZ (ETT), 06H03DZ (IVC device), 027Q3ZZ (pulmonary artery dilation / intervention), 3E043GC (thrombolytic infusion), 5A1D80Z (urinary filtration, prolonged intermittent <6 hrs/day), 5A2204Z (restoration of cardiac rhythm), and others. Summary determination and rationale (claim-level): - Supported as billed: I26.99 (massive pulmonary embolism), I46.9 (cardiac arrest with ROSC), J96.01 (acute hypoxemic respiratory failure), N17.9 (AKI), I82.401 (right femoral DVT, POA=N), and the procedures documenting airway placement, catheter-directed thrombolysis, IVC device placement, and defibrillation/ROSC are supported by the record. Cite: History & Physical (Admitting) and ED/Angiography notes documenting pulseless VT, ROSC after 15 minutes with three defibrillation attempts and ACLS (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, p. 312-821: "On EMS arrival the patient was in pulseless ventricular tachycardia. Return of spontaneous circulation was achieved after 15 minutes of CPR with three defibrillation attempts and multiple rounds of ACLS medications."), CT angiography confirming massive bilateral saddle PE (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, p. 312-821: "CT pulmonary angiography confirmed massive bilateral saddle pulmonary embolism with right heart strain."), and documentation of intubation/mechanical ventilation and catheter-directed thrombolysis (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, p. 312-821: "Given hemodynamic instability, catheter-directed thrombolysis was performed with tissue plasminogen activator.") and (Emergency Department Provider Note, Chart Notes, p. 312: "Emergency intubation performed. Rapid CT pulmonary angiography confirmed massive bilateral saddle PE... TTM initiated."). The J96.01 criteria are met by provider documentation of intubation/mechanical ventilation and ABG/oxygenation data (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, p. 312-821: "ABG pH 7.32 / PaCO2 34 / PaO2 65 on 100% FiO2." and Active Problem List: "6 | Acute respiratory failure with prolonged mechanical ventilation"). - Unsupported / materially discrepant (Finding): the claim includes an ICD-10-PCS procedure for urinary filtration / intermittent dialysis (5A1D80Z). The clinical documentation explicitly documents the AKI as "non-dialysis" and describes conservative management and recovery: History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, p. 312-821: "8 | Post-arrest AKI (KDIGO 2), non-dialysis, recovered" and Discharge / Transfer Summary, Transfer / Discharge Summary, p. 1011-1012: "The course was complicated by ... mild post-arrest AKI managed conservatively ... resolved AKI." At the same time, the facility's Billing & Coding Summary lists continuous renal replacement therapy / CRRT as a coded/billing item (Billing & Coding Summary, p. 756: "5A1D60Z | Continuous renal replacement (CRRT/CVVHDF) | Days 3-10"), which conflicts with the clinician charting that the AKI was non-dialysis. There is no procedure note, dialysis flowsheet, or physician/nephrology note retrieved that documents initiation of intermittent hemodialysis or any renal replacement therapy. Per the AKI policy, initiation of RRT would satisfy objective AKI staging (and would support an RRT procedure code) but that initiation must be documented (Policy Documents/DRG/Acute Kidney Injury.docx, Validation Criteria  Medical Pathway: "[1] Presumption rule: When the medical record documents initiation of renal replacement therapy ... Criterion 2 is presumed satisfied"). In this chart the explicit provider-level statement that the AKI was "non-dialysis" plus absence of any RRT procedure/note contradicts billing the dialysis procedure 5A1D80Z. Therefore the dialysis procedure line is unsupported and should be removed from the procedure set. - Secondary diagnostic issue (audit observation but not the basis for primary finding): G93.1 (anoxic brain damage) is billed as an MCC. The anoxic brain injury policy requires explicit provider documentation of anoxic brain injury (or objective neuroimaging/EEG/SSEP evidence or presumption rules when persistent coma/TTM/neuroprognostication is documented) (Policy Documents/DRG/Anoxic Brain Injury.docx, Validation Criteria  Medical Pathway: "1. Criterion 1 - Provider Documentation of Diagnosis: Provider documentation of anoxic brain injury ..." and criterion 2 objective evidence list). In this record the neurology consult and subsequent notes document an encouraging neurologic exam and "excellent neurologic recovery" (Neurology Consultation, Chart Notes, p. 79: "Post-arrest patient with encouraging early neurologic exam. Neuroprognostication at 72 hours indicated intact function with follow-up expected excellent."; Discharge / Transfer Summary, Transfer / Discharge Summary, p. 1011-1012: "excellent neurologic recovery post-arrest"). There is not an explicit clinician statement in the retrieved notes diagnosing "anoxic brain damage" or objective imaging/EEG/SSEP consistent with diffuse anoxic brain injury. Because the policy requires explicit attribution or objective findings to support G93.1, the documentation does not meet the policy's validation criteria to support G93.1 as an MCC. Therefore G93.1 is not supported for coding as anoxic brain damage and should be removed from the diagnosis list (the chart supports post-arrest cognitive dysfunction and a TTM course but not a provider-established diagnosis of anoxic brain injury in the retrieved notes). See Policy Documents/DRG/Anoxic Brain Injury.docx (Validation Criteria  Medical Pathway: "1. Criterion 1 - Provider Documentation of Diagnosis: Provider documentation of anoxic brain injury ..." which is required). What I am changing on the claim (complete corrected lists): - Remove procedure 5A1D80Z (urinary filtration / intermittent dialysis) because the clinician documentation explicitly documents AKI as "non-dialysis" and no RRT initiation is present in the chart. (If objective dialysis initiation documentation is produced on appeal, RRT coding could be re-instated.) - Remove diagnosis G93.1 (anoxic brain damage) because the record does not contain explicit provider documentation or objective neuroprognostic evidence meeting the policy's validation criteria for that diagnosis; the chart documents post-arrest syndrome and cognitive dysfunction with eventual excellent recovery, which does not meet the policy threshold for G93.1. Corrected / final diagnosis list (position 1 = principal): 1. I26.99 2. I46.9 3. J96.01 4. I50.30 5. N17.9 6. I82.401 7. E03.9 8. F32.9 9. Z86.73 10. Z79.01 11. Z95.81 Corrected / final procedure list (removed 5A1D80Z): 0BH17EZ, 02JYXZZ, 06H03DZ, 027Q3ZZ, 3E043GC, 02HV33Z, 03HY32Z, 5A2204Z Discharge disposition (as documented): "Destination: Acute Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility" (Transfer / Discharge Summary, Transfer / Discharge Summary, p. 1011-1012). Audit action: Remove unsupported procedure 5A1D80Z and remove unsupported diagnosis G93.1. Rationale and specific citations below support those changes. No provider query is required to demonstrate that cardiac arrest, PE, intubation, thrombolysis, and AKI (non-dialysis) occurred; those are well documented. If the provider can produce explicit chart documentation of dialysis initiation or a provider note explicitly diagnosing anoxic brain injury with the required objective evidence, the removed items can be reinstated on appeal.
rationale_letter: Dear Provider, Re: MR_23 - Inpatient claim level DRG audit determination We reviewed the medical record and billed codes for the above inpatient encounter. The audit compared the submitted diagnosis and procedure codes to the documentation in the medical record and to the applicable coding validation policies. Finding: Unsupported procedure and unsupported diagnosis (claim-level correction) Basis for Finding: 1) Dialysis / renal replacement therapy procedure (ICD-10-PCS 5A1D80Z) - unsupported. The clinical documentation explicitly records the acute kidney injury as "Post-arrest AKI (KDIGO 2), non-dialysis, recovered" and the discharge summary documents the AKI was managed conservatively and resolved (History & Physical (Admitting), Chart Notes, p. 312-821: "8 | Post-arrest AKI (KDIGO 2), non-dialysis, recovered"; Discharge / Transfer Summary, Transfer / Discharge Summary, p. 1011-1012: "...mild post-arrest AKI managed conservatively, and ... resolved AKI."). However, the claim/procedural coding includes an intermittent urinary filtration/dialysis code and the facility billing extract lists CRRT/renal replacement therapy codes. There is no dialysis procedure note, dialysis flowsheet, nephrology procedure documentation, or any objective documentation retrieved that documents initiation of renal replacement therapy. Per the AKI validation guidance, initiation of RRT must be documented to support coding of an RRT procedure (Policy Documents/DRG/Acute Kidney Injury.docx, Validation Criteria  Medical Pathway: "[1] Presumption rule: When the medical record documents initiation of renal replacement therapy (hemodialysis, CRRT, or peritoneal dialysis) during the encounter, Criterion 2 is presumed satisfied ..."). Because no such initiation is documented, the renal replacement procedure code(s) billed are not supported by the medical record and will be removed. 2) Anoxic brain damage (G93.1) - unsupported. The policy for anoxic brain injury requires explicit provider documentation attributing brain injury to hypoxic/anoxic events or objective neurological evidence (neuroimaging, EEG, SSEPs) or the presumption when prolonged coma/TTM with documented multimodal prognostication is present (Policy Documents/DRG/Anoxic Brain Injury.docx, Validation Criteria  Medical Pathway: "1. Criterion 1 - Provider Documentation of Diagnosis: Provider documentation of anoxic brain injury, hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, post-cardiac arrest brain injury ..."). In this record the neurology consult and subsequent notes document an encouraging neurologic exam and ultimate "excellent neurologic recovery" (Neurology Consultation, Chart Notes, p. 79: "Post-arrest patient with encouraging early neurologic exam. Neuroprognostication at 72 hours indicated intact function with follow-up expected excellent."; Discharge / Transfer Summary, p. 1011-1012: "excellent neurologic recovery post-arrest"). There is no explicit provider diagnosis of "anoxic brain damage" or objective neurodiagnostic evidence meeting the policy criteria in the retrieved documentation. Therefore G93.1 is not supported and will be removed. Correction being made: On the audited claim we will remove the unsupported procedure 5A1D80Z (urinary filtration / intermittent dialysis) and remove diagnosis G93.1 (anoxic brain damage). All other billed diagnoses and procedures reviewed (including I26.99 massive PE; I46.9 cardiac arrest with ROSC; J96.01 acute hypoxemic respiratory failure with mechanical ventilation and ABG support; IVC device placement; catheter-directed thrombolysis; endotracheal intubation; and the right lower extremity DVT) are documented and supported in the medical record and will remain on the claim. If you disagree with this determination, please provide the following within your appeal response: - For reinstating the dialysis procedure(s): the specific procedure note(s), dialysis flowsheet(s), nephrology progress note, or other contemporaneous documentation showing initiation and administration of renal replacement therapy during this encounter (date/time and modality), or an amended provider note stating RRT was initiated. - For reinstating G93.1: a provider-authored note explicitly documenting "anoxic brain injury" / "hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy" attributed to the qualifying event, or objective neurodiagnostic evidence (CT/MRI describing diffuse anoxic injury, EEG showing burst-suppression in post-anoxic context, or SSEPs) or a documented multimodal prognostication meeting the policy presumption criteria. Cited record excerpts and policy references are provided below for your convenience. Sincerely, Clinical Audit Team
